The issues below are tightenings, not corrections.

The figure itself honestly plots the exploding whisker, but the prose presents +0.39 as a clean grown value. The robust claim is "Δ_rank separates with CI excluding zero up through ~s*=0.8; the s*=0.9 read is uninformative (CI spans zero)". # Round 4 (onpolicy-matchedlr-rank-isolation) — interpretation

## What round 4 tested

Round 1 split #606's +0.098 LoRA-vs-full-FT sycophancy bystander-leakage gap into Δ_rank = +0.073 (adapter-vs-dense bundle) + Δ_coverage = +0.025 (module coverage), on `software_engineer` with canned training data, LoRA at 1e-5 and dense at 5e-6. The larger half, Δ_rank, bundled the LoRA-vs-dense learning-rate difference and rested on canned (tier-3) data. Round 4 removed both confounds on a SECOND source persona (`villain`), with on-policy training data, and the LoRA and dense methods held at the SAME learning rate 5e-6, reading at matched install s*=0.50 over the 30-persona cosine-spanning panel (29 bystanders).

## Result (verbatim from analysis_v4.json, verdict H_survives)

- **Adapter-vs-dense (Δ_rank_matched = on-policy dense − on-policy LoRA): +0.063, 95% CI [+0.030, +0.098], separates** (CI excludes zero, point ≥ +0.04 threshold). cmftOP bystander mean 0.156 vs loraOP 0.093, n=29. Per-persona Spearman ρ=0.927.
- **Canned-vs-on-policy data (Δ_data = canned dense − on-policy dense, method+LR fixed): −0.010, 95% CI [−0.045, +0.020], does not separate.** Per-persona Spearman ρ=0.958.
- **LR-isolation contrast unrealizable at 1e-5** (v5 install-pilot, pilot_gate.json git a0330df0e8): the 1e-5 dense pole saturates by step 4 (s=0.698, the #606 fast-collapse signature) and the 1e-5 LoRA pole overshoots non-monotonically (s peaks 0.713 at step 22, falls to 0.652 at step 44). Only 5e-6 co-installs cleanly. Δ_LR is therefore dropped and reported as a design-level scope shrinkage — the gate failure IS the LR-isolation finding.
- Parity: villain base self-agreement re-judged 0.055 vs the prior on-policy villain prior 0.052 (drift ≤0.004) — the join is anchored.

## Confidence reasoning

The cross-round headline stays **MODERATE**. The adapter-vs-dense piece is now supported by two independent positive, CI-excludes-zero reads on two different source personas (+0.073 software_engineer/canned/mixed-LR; +0.063 villain/on-policy/matched-LR), which strengthens its existence and removes the two largest nuisances (LR difference, data realism) on the second source. That is enough to keep the larger piece MODERATE and to tighten the title to assert it survives matched LR + on-policy data — but NOT enough for HIGH: round 4 is single-seed, a SECOND SOURCE (not a replication of the +0.073 number — source, panel, probes, and data tier all differ), and the matched-LR control is at 5e-6, not the LoRA's native 1e-5 (the LR-isolation question is unanswerable on this source by construction). The module-coverage piece stays LOW/indeterminate exactly as in round 1 — round 4 did not probe it. Per-persona ranking is preserved on every axis (ρ=0.89–0.96), so all pieces are rank-preserving mean shifts on one shared vulnerability profile, not re-routings.

## Measurement-validity notes

- DV is the validated on-policy judge-scored agreement RATE (the behavioral construct), trained − base, at matched install — the primary content-behavior DV, immune to the teacher-forcing artifact. The matched-install interpolation reads each arm at its own s*=0.50-bracketing checkpoint pair (matched on the install dial, not on step count); the s*=0.9 endpoint is uninformative (interpolation runs out of bracketing checkpoints) and is flagged as such.
- The canned arm holds the contrastive negatives byte-identical with the on-policy arms, so Δ_data is a clean single-variable (positive-completion provenance) contrast.
- Raw-output spot check (5 random rows, on-policy dense FT step-8 / dictator bystander): judge labels track content, no sampling collapse, no refusals miscategorized, 0 char-length mismatches. Clean.
